referents.why: Dative 'to them' is the crowd Pilate questions. The crowd is not offered as a candidate.
Neuter interrogative 'What evil' asks for the deed; it refers to no candidate.
Object 'Him' of 'Crucify' is Jesus, not offered as a candidate here. The builder's w2 is wrong, since Pilate is not the one crucified.
Implied 'he' who did the evil is Jesus, the person Pilate asks about. Jesus is not offered as a candidate in this verse.
The imperative 'Crucify' is spoken to Pilate, who has just asked the question; the implied singular 'you' is Pilate.

links.why: Pilate's question is nested in his saying clause, as the said words.
The imperative is nested inside the crowd's shouting clause, as the said words.

The connective before 'they shouted all the louder' is the separate word de, adversative, not a fused waw. The form does not support 'and then'. The relation the text carries is contrast, added below.
links.category: connective is not a fused waw

links.why: Pilate's saying introduces his question, which is what is said (R1).
The shouting introduces its command, which is what is said (R1).
The mid-verse adversative de: 'but they shouted all the louder' sets the crowd's cry against Pilate's question. The host is cl0.

groups.why: Pilate is the sender of the question in cl1. The addressee is the crowd, not offered as a candidate, so the addressee member is removed.
The sender of the shout is the crowd, not offered in this verse; the builder's w10 is 'King' from another verse and not a candidate here, so the sender member is removed. The addressee is Pilate.

none_fit.what: The implied third plural subject is not in the slot list. It is the crowd, not offered as a candidate.
